body:
Corroborating measurement from the #10086 dispatch (which touched this file to convert its entry guard).

This card says `scripts/pm/git-history.mjs --self-test` runs nowhere in CI. It is worth recording that the self-test is **currently red**, and has been for at least as long as `origin/main` @ 923c4247:

```text
$ node scripts/pm/git-history.mjs --self-test
  ✗ and the answer is the real one (21 commits: the daily fixture commits i=19..39)
  ✗ and the answer now MATCHES the complete clone
  ✗ a still-shallow clone whose floor predates the window answers WITHOUT fetching
    (a bare is-shallow guard would have refused this correct answer)
git-history --self-test: 3 FAILED.
```

Measured on **unmodified `origin/main`** in a clean worktree, and byte-identically on the #10086 branch — so it is not caused by that change. The remote was reachable from the container (`git ls-remote` succeeded), so this is not simply "no network"; the three failing cases are the shallow-clone deepening fixture, and the failing assertion names a *daily* commit window (`i=19..39`), which suggests time-dependence rather than a hard break.

That sharpens this card's argument rather than adding a new one: the gap named here is not hypothetical. A self-test that no CI job runs has had three red cases sitting in it, and nothing reported them — which is the same silence-reads-as-pass shape, one level up. Whoever wires it should expect it to go red on the first run and budget for fixing the fixture, not just for the wiring.

Filed as a comment rather than a new issue because the subject is this file's self-test, which is what this card is about.

Input for the detector this card proposes, derived while doing the root `scripts/**` half in PR #10649. Recording it here because that PR closes its own card, and the two things this card will need — **the predicate** and **the reasoned opt-out list** — would go with it.

### 1. The predicate matters more than the alias resolution

`--self-test` *appearing* in a file is not the same as a file *shipping* one. On today's `main`, matching the mention gives **92** root `scripts/*.mjs`; requiring an actual `process.argv` branch for the flag gives **83**. The nine-file gap is real files that only discuss the flag in prose — `adr-anchors.mjs`, `eslint-fatal-guard.mjs`, `regen-artifacts.mjs` among them — and a gate built on the mention will demand wiring for tools that have nothing to run.

The consequence is not academic: the sub-card's table was built on the looser predicate and reported 87 shipping / 6 unreached where the stricter one gives **82 / 9 at that same commit**. Both columns moved, and two genuinely unreached scripts were missing from the list.

Suggested predicate: strip block and line comments, then require `argv` within ~60 chars of a `'--self-test'` literal.

### 2. The reasoned opt-out list, for root `scripts/**`

After PR #10649 wires four (`ts-parse.mjs`, `js-comment-mask.mjs`, `invoked-as.mjs`, `check-optional-error-sink-contract.mjs`), **four remain unreached and each is deliberate**:

| script | why it should be an opt-out, not a wiring |
|---|---|
| `setup-git-hooks.mjs` | Its `--self-test` asserts a property of **the current clone** (`core.hooksPath` + two merge-driver settings), not of the committed tree. Its header states the registrar warns and exits 0 on every failure path so that "CI images that install with `--ignore-scripts`" are not broken. Wiring it reds a required context on an environment fact no PR changed. |
| `checklist-select.mjs` | Reachable only via `check:platform-checklist`, which `lint.yml` already documents as excluded **by maintainer decision** — "it runs on a periodic manual cadence … a QA ledger, not a code gate". A detector that demands it re-opens a lane a ruling closed. |
| `measure-test-shard-timings.mjs` | A by-hand generator over `.turbo/runs/` artifacts; its product is committed and the **consumer** side is already pinned in CI (`partition-test-shards.mjs --self-test` at `lint.yml:1367`, and `loadTimings()` refuses a missing or malformed dataset rather than falling back). |
| `ablation-dist-preflight.mjs` | The closest call. Cost is not the argument (~0.07 s). Left because no CI gate consumes it and no gate's design argument delegates to it — its consumers are agents, not workflows. Worth revisiting if that changes. |

The first two are the interesting ones for the gate's shape: an opt-out list that cannot express "this is an environment assertion" or "a ruling excluded this lane" will get argued with rather than maintained.

### 3. Affordability, which this card flags as unmeasured

Measured for the four now wired: **~14 s total per PR**, of which `ts-parse.mjs --self-test` is ~10 s because it spawns ~20 real node children (the spawns are the pin — a caller's `try`/`catch` must not be able to swallow the refusal). The sub-card budgeted ~4 s for it, so a detector that lands more of these should assume roughly 2.5x its own estimate. None of the four needs network.

Closing as **already fixed** — premise re-derived at `origin/main` = `01c50322a1` (fetched 2026-08-21T10:51:38Z), before dispatch.

`scripts/pm/git-history.mjs --self-test` **does** run in CI now. It landed in **#10506** (commit `7f8b36086f`, 2026-08-21T02:10:05Z) as the first line of the `Shallow-history guard self-tests` step:

```yaml
# .github/workflows/lint.yml:530-535
- name: Shallow-history guard self-tests
  run: |
    node scripts/pm/git-history.mjs --self-test
    node scripts/check-engine-split-ratio.mjs --self-test
    bash scripts/collect-release-notes.sh --self-test
```

That PR was not aimed at this card, but its comment at `lint.yml:518` states this card's observation in its own words:

> `git-history.mjs` is listed first and deliberately: it is the shared predicate all three call, it shipped for #9878 with a self-test that until now NOTHING in this repo ran, and an unrun self-test is a phantom check

It also independently reached this card's conclusion about the *route*: it invokes the tool as `node` rather than adding a `pnpm check:*` alias, **because root `package.json` is declared territory of the @changesets/cli v3 migration lane (#9465)** while that lane runs. So the fix took the only shape available, and a dispatch against this card today would have collided with #9465's fence before it collided with anything else.

Two things worth recording rather than losing with the card:

1. **The sixth instance closed itself, still one at a time.** This card argued the class has been closed five times individually (#8110, #8170, #8162, #8528, #9348) and that no gate has ever found one. That is still true — #10506 found it the same way all six were found: a human or agent noticing while doing something adjacent. Nothing in this repo yet asserts *"every `--self-test` a tool ships is run by something."* If that gate is worth having, it is a separate card and it should be filed as one; this card's closure is not evidence the class is retired.
2. **`check-engine-split-ratio.mjs` and `collect-release-notes.sh` were swept in alongside it**, neither of which appeared in this card's table — so the unwired population at filing time was larger than the one instance measured here. That is the ordinary shape of a hand-kept census, and the reason for point 1.

No code change was needed. Dropping `pm:queue`; not dispatched, so no `pm:dispatched` was ever applied.
